package_info.package_versions: all published versions in this campaign
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a setup.py file with a base64-encoded PowerShell payload that, when executed during installation, downloads and executes a Windows trojan from a remote Dropbox URL. The package is part of a coordinated campaign, with multiple packages published under arbitrary names, all containing identical malicious payloads designed to compromise Windows systems by delivering and executing remote malware.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Executes a PowerShell command that downloads a Windows executable (Esquele.exe) from a Dropbox URL, saves it as WindowsCache.exe in the user's home directory, and immediately executes the downloaded binary.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code leverages setup.py to execute a PowerShell command that downloads and runs an external executable from Dropbox during package installation, a well-known malware delivery tactic. The use of base64 encoding and obfuscation further indicates intent to evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: setup.py should only handle package installation logic, such as dependency management or build steps. It should never download and execute arbitrary binaries from untrusted sources, especially without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may download pre-built binaries or dependencies, but only from trusted, verified sources and with explicit user awareness. Automatic execution of downloaded files from third-party file hosting services is never acceptable in legitimate packages.
key_indicators: Base64-encoded or obfuscated PowerShell payload embedded in setup.py
Execution of PowerShell commands from Python install scripts
Network request to Dropbox (dl.dropbox.com) for downloading an executable
Creation of WindowsCache.exe (or update.exe) in user directories during install
Immediate execution of the downloaded binary as part of the installation process

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious PyPI package (e.g., nvidiapaypalsuper), triggering execution of setup.py.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of the embedded PowerShell payload

attack_chain.action: The PowerShell command downloads a Windows trojan (Esquele.exe) from a Dropbox URL and saves it as WindowsCache.exe in the user's home directory.
attack_chain.leads_to: Downloaded trojan is written to disk

attack_chain.action: The downloaded trojan (WindowsCache.exe) is immediately executed, potentially performing spyware, info-stealing, or other malicious activities on the victim's system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Compromise of the victim's Windows system

behavioral_signatures: setup.py executing PowerShell or other shell commands during package installation
Package installation process initiating network requests to external file hosting services (e.g., Dropbox)
Automatic download and execution of binaries (e.g., WindowsCache.exe) as part of install process
Presence of base64-encoded or obfuscated code in setup.py
file_indicators: setup.py containing base64-encoded or obfuscated PowerShell payloads
Creation of WindowsCache.exe or update.exe in user directories (e.g., C:\Users\<username>\WindowsCache.exe)
setup.py scripts invoking os.system or subprocess to run PowerShell
network_indicators: Any outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to Dropbox or similar file hosting services during package installation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for PyPI package installations that invoke PowerShell or shell commands from setup.py, especially those that download and execute files from external sources. Flag any setup.py scripts containing base64-encoded or obfuscated payloads. Watch for network activity to known malicious URLs (e.g., Dropbox links) during package installation. Alert on the creation and execution of suspicious binaries (e.g., WindowsCache.exe) in user directories immediately after package installation. Correlate these behaviors to identify coordinated malware campaigns using arbitrary package names.
